text:
Lee Zeldin, administrator of the Environmental Protection Agency, praised President Donald Trump's efforts to roll back methane emissions regulations Thursday on Newsmax.

Trump said Tuesday that his administration was "terminating" a Biden-era rule aimed at cutting planet-warming methane emissions from oil and natural gas operations.

At a campaign rally in Texas, Trump said the change would save consumers and energy producers $45 billion and yield an added 210 million barrels of oil. That volume is equivalent to about 10 days of U.S. petroleum consumption.

Zeldin said this would strengthen American energy dominance.

"It's important for our environment too," Zeldin said on "Carl Higbie: FRONTLINE." "Because we tap into our supplies, it's so much better for our environment than so many other countries elsewhere around the world."

"This is a big deal: $45 billion in regulatory savings, unleashing a tremendous amount of U.S. oil production and natural gas production," he added. "I'll tell you, one thing that's really simple to understand is that where you see the largest increases in energy costs, they're in the blue states."

The EPA administrator argued that stricter energy regulations in Democrat-led states contribute to higher energy costs than in Republican-led states.

"This is no coincidence," Zeldin said. "It's about policy at the state and local level.

"It's about unleashing reliable, durable baseload power instead of trying to regulate out of existence this baseload power that warms homes, that fuels your vehicles and your small businesses, that keeps you cool in the summer."

"Everything that is important for our quality of life, for our cost of living, the trucks that deliver our goods, the list goes on," he added. "There are so many Americans who are leaders at a state and local level who get it."

"Unfortunately, there are others in places like New York and California and elsewhere where they want to talk about intermittent sources as if it's a substitute for baseload power," Zeldin continued. "If you regulate this stuff out of existence, the Americans who need the help the most, they're the ones who suffer the most."

Zeldin said the Trump administration has been able to protect the environment and grow the economy.

"It's not a choice between the two," Zeldin said. "At the Biden EPA, it was a choice where they said, in order to protect the environment, we have to strangulate entire sectors of our economy out of existence.

"We can and must do both. The American public demand it, and they demand common sense when doing it."

Planned $950 million HJT facility is expected to add 4 GW of annual solar cell manufacturing capacity and create more than 700 local jobs

HOUSTON, Oct. 29, 2026 /CNW/ -- SEG Solar ("SEG"), a leading global vertically integrated solar manufacturer, today announced that it has signed a land agreement for a planned $950 million, 4 GW heterojunction (HJT) solar cell plant at its Tomball Industrial Campus in the greater Houston area.

The facility is expected to create more than 700 local jobs and is planned to come online in two 2 GW phases, targeted for 2028 and 2029. It would make the SEG Tomball Industrial Campus one of the only U.S. manufacturing locations where HJT cells, modules, and key components are made in one place.

The facility will be located adjacent to SEG's existing 4 GW Tomball #1 module manufacturing facility and its 4.6 GW Tomball #2 module manufacturing facility currently under construction. Once completed, the HJT cell facility will bring solar cell, module and key component manufacturing together at SEG's Tomball campus, alongside warehousing, an R&D center, a certified testing laboratory, and planned EVA and junction box production lines.

SEG's Texas-made modules, built with U.S.-produced HJT cells, will help developers and asset owners meet domestic content requirements while improving project economics. They will also provide something increasingly valuable in today's market: a dependable source of U.S.-manufactured supply.

Jim Wood, chief executive officer of SEG Solar, said "Bringing HJT cell manufacturing to the U.S. will give customers a more domestic supply chain with clearer sourcing and a single company standing behind the product. As the only U.S. company dedicated to integrated domestic vertical manufacturing, SEG will continue to strengthen our U.S. operations and innovation. American-made cells, American-made modules, one company accountable."

About SEG Solar

Founded in 2021, SEG is a leading vertically integrated PV manufacturer headquartered in Houston, Texas, U.S., and is dedicated to delivering reliable and cost-effective solar modules to the utility, commercial, and residential markets. By the end of 2025, SEG had shipped over 7.5 GW of solar modules worldwide and reached a module production capacity of 6.5 GW.
